sanskrit: tac chrutvā cābruvan devāḥ sahasrākṣam idaṃ vacaḥ vareṇa cchandyatāṃ śakra rājarṣir yadi śakyate
english: Hearing this, the gods spoke these words to the thousand-eyed one: "Let the royal sage be appeased with a boon, O Śakra, if it can be done."

sanskrit: yadi hy atra pramītā vai svargaṃ gacchanti mānavāḥ asmān aniṣṭvā kratubhir bhāgo no na bhaviṣyati
english: "For if men who die in this place go straight to heaven without honoring us through sacrifices, then no share of the offerings will be left for us."

sanskrit: āgamya ca tataḥ śakras tadā rājarṣim abravīt alaṃ khedena bhavataḥ kriyatāṃ vacanaṃ mama
english: So Śakra came and spoke then to the royal sage: "Enough of your toil! Let my word be carried out."

sanskrit: mānavā ye nirāhārā dehaṃ tyakṣyanty atandritāḥ yudhi vā nihatāḥ samyag api tiryaggatā nṛpa
english: "Those men who, forgoing food, untiringly cast off the body, or who are duly slain in battle, even those gone to the state of beasts, O king—"

sanskrit: te svargabhājo rājendra bhavantv iti mahāmate tathāstv iti tato rājā kuruḥ śakram uvāca ha
english: "—let them become partakers of heaven, O lord of kings, O great-minded one." "So be it," said King Kuru then to Śakra in reply.

sanskrit: tatas tam abhyanujñāpya prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā jagāma tridivaṃ bhūyaḥ kṣipraṃ balaniṣūdanaḥ
english: Then, having taken his leave, the slayer of Bala, his inmost soul rejoicing, swiftly returned once more to the realm of heaven.

sanskrit: evam etad yaduśreṣṭha kṛṣṭaṃ rājarṣiṇā purā śakreṇa cāpy anujñātaṃ puṇyaṃ prāṇān vimuñcatām
english: Thus it was, O best of the Yadus, that this field was plowed of old by the royal sage, and Śakra too granted that it should be holy for those who release their breath here.

sanskrit: api cātra svayaṃ śakro jagau gāthāṃ surādhipaḥ kurukṣetre nibaddhāṃ vai tāṃ śṛṇuṣva halāyudha
english: And here Śakra himself, the lord of the gods, sang a verse composed about Kurukṣetra; hear it, O wielder of the plow.

sanskrit: pāṃsavo 'pi kurukṣetrād vāyunā samudīritāḥ api duṣkṛtakarmāṇaṃ nayanti paramāṃ gatim
english: "Even the dust-grains from Kurukṣetra, stirred up by the wind, lead even the doer of evil deeds to the supreme goal."

sanskrit: surarṣabhā brāhmaṇasattamāś ca; tathā nṛgādyā naradevamukhyāḥ iṣṭvā mahārhaiḥ kratubhir nṛsiṃha; saṃnyasya dehān sugatiṃ prapannāḥ
english: Bulls among the gods and the most excellent of brāhmaṇas, and Nṛga and other chiefs among god-like kings, O lion among men, having worshiped with costly sacrifices and laid down their bodies, attained the blessed goal.

sanskrit: tarantukārantukayor yad antaraṃ; rāmahradānāṃ ca macakrukasya etat kurukṣetrasamantapañcakaṃ; prajāpater uttaravedir ucyate
english: That which lies between Tarantuka and Arantuka, and between the lakes of Rāma and Macakruka—this Samantapañcaka of Kurukṣetra is called the upper altar of Prajāpati.

sanskrit: śivaṃ mahat puṇyam idaṃ divaukasāṃ; susaṃmataṃ svargaguṇaiḥ samanvitam ataś ca sarve 'pi vasuṃdharādhipā; hatā gamiṣyanti mahātmanāṃ gatim
english: Auspicious, great, and holy is this place, honored by the dwellers of heaven, endowed with the virtues of the celestial realm; and therefore all the lords of the earth, when slain here, shall go to the goal of great souls.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kurukṣetraṃ tato dṛṣṭvā dattvā dāyāṃś ca sātvataḥ āśramaṃ sumahad divyam agamaj janamejaya
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having then beheld Kurukṣetra and bestowed gifts, the Sātvata went on to a very great and divine hermitage, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: madhūkāmravanopetaṃ plakṣanyagrodhasaṃkulam ciribilvayutaṃ puṇyaṃ panasārjunasaṃkulam
english: It was furnished with groves of madhūka and mango, thick with plakṣa and banyan trees, holy, set about with ciribilva, and crowded with panasa and arjuna trees.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā yādavaśreṣṭhaḥ pravaraṃ puṇyalakṣaṇam papraccha tān ṛṣīn sarvān kasyāśramavaras tv ayam
english: Beholding it, foremost in holy marks, the best of the Yādavas asked all those sages: "Whose excellent hermitage is this?"

sanskrit: te tu sarve mahātmānam ūcū rājan halāyudham śṛṇu vistarato rāma yasyāyaṃ pūrvam āśramaḥ
english: And they all said to the great-souled wielder of the plow, O king: "Hear in full, O Rāma, whose hermitage this was of old."

sanskrit: atra viṣṇuḥ purā devas taptavāṃs tapa uttamam atrāsya vidhivad yajñāḥ sarve vṛttāḥ sanātanāḥ
english: "Here in days past the god Viṣṇu performed supreme austerity; here all his eternal sacrifices were duly carried out."

sanskrit: atraiva brāhmaṇī siddhā kaumārabrahmacāriṇī yogayuktā divaṃ yātā tapaḥsiddhā tapasvinī
english: "Here too a brāhmaṇa woman, perfected, chaste from girlhood, joined to yoga and accomplished in austerity, the ascetic went to heaven."

sanskrit: babhūva śrīmatī rājañ śāṇḍilyasya mahātmanaḥ sutā dhṛtavratā sādhvī niyatā brahmacāriṇī
english: "She was the illustrious daughter of the great-souled Śāṇḍilya, O king—firm in her vows, virtuous, disciplined, and chaste."

sanskrit: sā tu prāpya paraṃ yogaṃ gatā svargam anuttamam bhuktvāśrame 'śvamedhasya phalaṃ phalavatāṃ śubhā gatā svargaṃ mahābhāgā pūjitā niyatātmabhiḥ
english: "Having attained the highest yoga, she went to the supreme heaven; the blessed one, having enjoyed in that hermitage the fruit of the horse-sacrifice among those who reap reward, the highly fortunate one went to heaven, honored by the self-controlled."

sanskrit: abhigamyāśramaṃ puṇyaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca yadupuṃgavaḥ ṛṣīṃs tān abhivādyātha pārśve himavato 'cyutaḥ skandhāvārāṇi sarvāṇi nivartyāruruhe 'calam
english: Having approached and beheld the holy hermitage, the bull of the Yadus, that unfailing one, then saluting those sages, sent back all his encampments and ascended the mountain on the slope of the Himavat.

sanskrit: nātidūraṃ tato gatvā nagaṃ tāladhvajo balī puṇyaṃ tīrthavaraṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ
english: Going not far thence up the mountain, the mighty one whose banner bears the palm beheld a holy and excellent ford, and was filled with utmost wonder.

sanskrit: prabhavaṃ ca sarasvatyāḥ plakṣaprasravaṇaṃ balaḥ saṃprāptaḥ kārapacanaṃ tīrthapravaram uttamam
english: And Bala reached the source of the Sarasvatī, the spring of the plakṣa tree, and Kārapacana, the foremost and most excellent of fords.

sanskrit: halāyudhas tatra cāpi dattvā dānaṃ mahābalaḥ āplutaḥ salile śīte tasmāc cāpi jagāma ha āśramaṃ paramaprīto mitrasya varuṇasya ca
english: There too the mighty wielder of the plow bestowed gifts, bathed in the cold water, and thence, greatly pleased, went on to the hermitage of Mitra and Varuṇa.

sanskrit: indro 'gnir aryamā caiva yatra prāk prītim āpnuvan taṃ deśaṃ kārapacanād yamunāyāṃ jagāma ha
english: To that region where Indra, Agni, and Aryaman of old found their delight, on the Yamunā, he went from Kārapacana.

sanskrit: snātvā tatrāpi dharmātmā parāṃ tuṣṭim avāpya ca ṛṣibhiś caiva siddhaiś ca sahito vai mahābalaḥ upaviṣṭaḥ kathāḥ śubhrāḥ śuśrāva yadupuṃgavaḥ
english: Bathing there too, the righteous one attained supreme contentment; and the mighty bull of the Yadus, seated together with sages and perfected ones, listened to glorious tales.

sanskrit: tathā tu tiṣṭhatāṃ teṣāṃ nārado bhagavān ṛṣiḥ ājagāmātha taṃ deśaṃ yatra rāmo vyavasthitaḥ
english: And while they were tarrying thus, the blessed sage Nārada came to that region where Rāma was stationed.

sanskrit: jaṭāmaṇḍalasaṃvītaḥ svarṇacīrī mahātapāḥ hemadaṇḍadharo rājan kamaṇḍaludharas tathā
english: Wrapped in a coil of matted locks, clad in golden bark, of great austerity, bearing a golden staff, O king, and carrying a water-pot as well,

sanskrit: kacchapīṃ sukhaśabdāṃ tāṃ gṛhya vīṇāṃ manoramām nṛtye gīte ca kuśalo devabrāhmaṇapūjitaḥ
english: holding that lovely lute named Kacchapī of sweet sound, skilled in dance and song, honored by gods and brāhmaṇas,

sanskrit: prakartā kalahānāṃ ca nityaṃ ca kalahapriyaḥ taṃ deśam agamad yatra śrīmān rāmo vyavasthitaḥ
english: a stirrer-up of quarrels and ever fond of strife, he came to that region where the illustrious Rāma was stationed.

sanskrit: pratyutthāya tu te sarve pūjayitvā yatavratam devarṣiṃ paryapṛcchanta yathāvṛttaṃ kurūn prati
english: Rising up, they all paid honor to that one of restrained vows, and questioned the divine sage about what had befallen the Kurus.

sanskrit: tato 'syākathayad rājan nāradaḥ sarvadharmavit sarvam eva yathāvṛttam atītaṃ kurusaṃkṣayam
english: Then, O king, Nārada, knower of all dharmas, recounted to him all just as it had happened—the past destruction of the Kurus.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd rauhiṇeyo nāradaṃ dīnayā girā kim avasthaṃ tu tat kṣatraṃ ye ca tatrābhavan nṛpāḥ
english: Then the son of Rohiṇī said to Nārada in a sorrowful voice: "In what state now is that warrior caste, and the kings who were there?"

sanskrit: śrutam etan mayā pūrvaṃ sarvam eva tapodhana vistaraśravaṇe jātaṃ kautūhalam atīva me
english: "All this I have heard before, O wealth of austerity, yet a great eagerness has arisen in me to hear it in full."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca pūrvam eva hato bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sindhupatis tathā hato vaikartanaḥ karṇaḥ putrāś cāsya mahārathāḥ
english: Nārada said: Bhīṣma was slain at the very first, and Droṇa, and the lord of the Sindhus likewise; Karṇa, son of Vikartana, was slain, and his sons, the great chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: bhūriśravā rauhiṇeya madrarājaś ca vīryavān ete cānye ca bahavas tatra tatra mahābalāḥ
english: Bhūriśravas, O son of Rohiṇī, and the valiant king of the Madras—these and many other mighty ones, here and there,

sanskrit: priyān prāṇān parityajya priyārthaṃ kauravasya vai rājāno rājaputrāś ca samareṣv anivartinaḥ
english: kings and princes who never turned back in battles, laid down their own dear lives for the sake of the Kaurava's pleasure.

sanskrit: ahatāṃs tu mahābāho śṛṇu me tatra mādhava dhārtarāṣṭrabale śeṣāḥ kṛpo bhojaś ca vīryavān aśvatthāmā ca vikrānto bhagnasainyā diśo gatāḥ
english: But hear from me, O mighty-armed Mādhava, who there are not slain: those remaining in the host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son—Kṛpa, the valiant Bhoja, and the mighty Aśvatthāman—their army broken, have scattered to the directions.

sanskrit: duryodhano hate sainye pradruteṣu kṛpādiṣu hradaṃ dvaipāyanaṃ nāma viveśa bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ
english: His army slain, and Kṛpa and the others fled, Duryodhana, sorely grieved, entered the lake named Dvaipāyana.

sanskrit: śayānaṃ dhārtarāṣṭraṃ tu stambhite salile tadā pāṇḍavāḥ saha kṛṣṇena vāgbhir ugrābhir ārdayan
english: As the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra lay there, the waters frozen still, the Pāṇḍavas, together with Kṛṣṇa, tormented him with fierce words.

sanskrit: sa tudyamāno balavān vāgbhī rāma samantataḥ utthitaḥ prāg ghradād vīraḥ pragṛhya mahatīṃ gadām
english: Goaded on every side by their words, O Rāma, the mighty hero rose up at last from the lake, seizing his great mace.

sanskrit: sa cāpy upagato yuddhaṃ bhīmena saha sāṃpratam bhaviṣyati ca tat sadyas tayo rāma sudāruṇam
english: And even now he has come to combat with Bhīma; and forthwith, O Rāma, a most terrible fight between the two shall take place.

sanskrit: yadi kautūhalaṃ te 'sti vraja mādhava mā ciram paśya yuddhaṃ mahāghoraṃ śiṣyayor yadi manyase
english: If you have any curiosity, go, O Mādhava, without delay; behold the most dreadful fight of your two pupils, if you are so inclined.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā tān abhyarcya dvijarṣabhān sarvān visarjayām āsa ye tenābhyāgatāḥ saha gamyatāṃ dvārakāṃ ceti so 'nvaśād anuyāyinaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard Nārada's words and honored those bulls among brāhmaṇas, he dismissed all who had come there with him, and commanded his followers, "Let us go to Dvārakā."

sanskrit: so 'vatīryācalaśreṣṭhāt plakṣaprasravaṇāc chubhāt tataḥ prītamanā rāmaḥ śrutvā tīrthaphalaṃ mahat viprāṇāṃ saṃnidhau ślokam agāyad idam acyutaḥ
english: Descending from the best of mountains, from the auspicious spring of the plakṣa tree, then Rāma, glad of heart, having heard of the great fruit of the ford, sang in the presence of the brāhmaṇas this verse, that unfailing one:

sanskrit: sarasvatīvāsasamā kuto ratiḥ; sarasvatīvāsasamāḥ kuto guṇāḥ sarasvatīṃ prāpya divaṃ gatā janāḥ; sadā smariṣyanti nadīṃ sarasvatīm
english: "Where is delight to equal dwelling by the Sarasvatī? Where are virtues to equal dwelling by the Sarasvatī? Men who have gained the Sarasvatī and gone to heaven shall ever remember the river Sarasvatī."

sanskrit: sarasvatī sarvanadīṣu puṇyā; sarasvatī lokasukhāvahā sadā sarasvatīṃ prāpya janāḥ suduṣkṛtāḥ; sadā na śocanti paratra ceha ca
english: "The Sarasvatī is holy among all rivers; the Sarasvatī ever brings happiness to the world. Men, even doers of grievous deeds, having gained the Sarasvatī, never grieve, in the world beyond or here."

sanskrit: tato muhur muhuḥ prītyā prekṣamāṇaḥ sarasvatīm hayair yuktaṃ rathaṃ śubhram ātiṣṭhata paraṃtapaḥ
english: Then, gazing again and again with affection upon the Sarasvatī, the scorcher of foes mounted his gleaming chariot yoked with horses.

sanskrit: sa śīghragāminā tena rathena yadupuṃgavaḥ didṛkṣur abhisaṃprāptaḥ śiṣyayuddham upasthitam
english: With that swift-going chariot the bull of the Yadus, eager to see, arrived where the combat of his pupils was at hand.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ tad abhavad yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ janamejaya yatra duḥkhānvito rājā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bravīd idam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus did that tumultuous combat come about, O Janamejaya, concerning which the grief-stricken King Dhṛtarāṣṭra spoke these words.

sanskrit: rāmaṃ saṃnihitaṃ dṛṣṭvā gadāyuddha upasthite mama putraḥ kathaṃ bhīmaṃ pratyayudhyata saṃjaya
english: "When the mace-combat was at hand and Rāma seen present, how did my son fight back against Bhīma, O Saṃjaya?"

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca rāmasāṃnidhyam āsādya putro duryodhanas tava yuddhakāmo mahābāhuḥ samahṛṣyata vīryavān
english: Saṃjaya said: Coming into Rāma's presence, your son Duryodhana, mighty-armed and valiant, eager for combat, rejoiced greatly.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā lāṅgalinaṃ rājā pratyutthāya ca bhārata prītyā paramayā yukto yudhiṣṭhiram athābravīt
english: Beholding the plow-bearer, the king rose up, O descendant of Bharata, and, filled with utmost joy, then said to Yudhiṣṭhira:

sanskrit: samantapañcakaṃ kṣipram ito yāma viśāṃ pate prathitottaravedī sā devaloke prajāpateḥ
english: "Let us go swiftly from here to Samantapañcaka, O lord of peoples—that renowned upper altar of Prajāpati in the world of the gods."

sanskrit: tasmin mahāpuṇyatame trailokyasya sanātane saṃgrāme nidhanaṃ prāpya dhruvaṃ svargo bhaviṣyati
english: "In that most holy and eternal place of the three worlds, one who meets his death in battle shall surely attain heaven."

sanskrit: tathety uktvā mahārāja kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ samantapañcakaṃ vīraḥ prāyād abhimukhaḥ prabhuḥ
english: Saying "So be it," O great king, the heroic lord Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, set out facing toward Samantapañcaka.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā pragṛhya mahatīṃ gadām padbhyām amarṣād dyutimān agacchat pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: Then King Duryodhana, the resplendent one, seizing his great mace, went on foot in his wrath along with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tathā yāntaṃ gadāhastaṃ varmaṇā cāpi daṃśitam antarikṣagatā devāḥ sādhu sādhv ity apūjayan vātikāś ca narā ye 'tra dṛṣṭvā te harṣam āgatāḥ
english: As he went thus, mace in hand and clad in armor, the gods who move in the sky honored him crying "Well done! Well done!"; and what men of the air there were, beholding him, were filled with joy.

sanskrit: sa pāṇḍavaiḥ parivṛtaḥ kururājas tavātmajaḥ mattasyeva gajendrasya gatim āsthāya so 'vrajat
english: Surrounded by the Pāṇḍavas, the Kuru king, your son, went forward, assuming the gait of a rutting lordly elephant.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkhaninādena bherīṇāṃ ca mahāsvanaiḥ siṃhanādaiś ca śūrāṇāṃ diśaḥ sarvāḥ prapūritāḥ
english: Then with the blare of conches, the great din of kettledrums, and the lion-roars of the heroes, all the directions were filled.

sanskrit: pratīcyabhimukhaṃ deśaṃ yathoddiṣṭaṃ sutena te gatvā ca taiḥ parikṣiptaṃ samantāt sarvatodiśam
english: Having gone to the westward-facing region as designated by your son, it was encircled by them on every side, in all directions.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇena sarasvatyāḥ svayanaṃ tīrtham uttamam tasmin deśe tv aniriṇe tatra yuddham arocayan
english: To the south of the Sarasvatī lay an excellent ford named Samanta; in that region, on ground free of barren salt, they resolved to do battle.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahākoṭiṃ gadāṃ gṛhyātha varmabhṛt bibhrad rūpaṃ mahārāja sadṛśaṃ hi garutmataḥ
english: Then Bhīma, clad in armor, taking up his mace of vast bulk, bore a form, O great king, like unto Garutmat.

sanskrit: avabaddhaśirastrāṇaḥ saṃkhye kāñcanavarmabhṛt rarāja rājan putras te kāñcanaḥ śailarāḍ iva
english: His helm bound on, wearing golden armor in the fray, your son shone forth, O king, like a golden king of mountains.

sanskrit: varmabhyāṃ saṃvṛtau vīrau bhīmaduryodhanāv ubhau saṃyuge ca prakāśete saṃrabdhāv iva kuñjarau
english: Both heroes, Bhīma and Duryodhana, encased in their armor, shone in the combat like two enraged elephants.

sanskrit: raṇamaṇḍalamadhyasthau bhrātarau tau nararṣabhau aśobhetāṃ mahārāja candrasūryāv ivoditau
english: Standing in the midst of the battle-circle, those two bulls among men, the kinsmen, shone, O great king, like the risen moon and sun.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ nirīkṣetāṃ kruddhāv iva mahādvipau dahantau locanai rājan parasparavadhaiṣiṇau
english: They glared at each other like two angry mighty elephants, burning each other with their eyes, O king, each seeking the other's death.

sanskrit: saṃprahṛṣṭamanā rājan gadām ādāya kauravaḥ sṛkkiṇī saṃlihan rājan krodharaktekṣaṇaḥ śvasan
english: With exultant heart, O king, the Kaurava took up his mace, licking the corners of his mouth, his eyes red with wrath, breathing hard.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā gadām ādāya vīryavān bhīmasenam abhiprekṣya gajo gajam ivāhvayat
english: Then the valiant King Duryodhana, taking up his mace and looking toward Bhīmasena, challenged him as one elephant challenges another.

sanskrit: adrisāramayīṃ bhīmas tathaivādāya vīryavān āhvayām āsa nṛpatiṃ siṃhaḥ siṃhaṃ yathā vane
english: Likewise the valiant Bhīma, taking up his mace forged of the essence of the mountains, challenged the king as one lion challenges another in the forest.

sanskrit: tāv udyatagadāpāṇī duryodhanavṛkodarau saṃyuge sma prakāśete girī saśikharāv iva
english: With maces raised in their hands, Duryodhana and Wolf-belly shone in the fray like two mountains crowned with peaks.

sanskrit: tāv ubhāv abhisaṃkruddhāv ubhau bhīmaparākramau ubhau śiṣyau gadāyuddhe rauhiṇeyasya dhīmataḥ
english: Both were exceedingly enraged, both of terrible prowess, both pupils in mace-combat of the wise son of Rohiṇī.

sanskrit: ubhau sadṛśakarmāṇau yamavāsavayor iva tathā sadṛśakarmāṇau varuṇasya mahābalau
english: Both were alike in their deeds, like Yama and Vāsava, and likewise the two mighty ones matched the deeds of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: vāsudevasya rāmasya tathā vaiśravaṇasya ca sadṛśau tau mahārāja madhukaiṭabhayor yudhi
english: Those two, O great king, were the equals of Vāsudeva, of Rāma, and of Vaiśravaṇa, and of Madhu and Kaiṭabha in combat.

sanskrit: ubhau sadṛśakarmāṇau raṇe sundopasundayoḥ tathaiva kālasya samau mṛtyoś caiva paraṃtapau
english: Both were alike in their deeds in battle to Sunda and Upasunda, and the two scorchers of foes were equal as well to Time and to Death.

sanskrit: anyonyam abhidhāvantau mattāv iva mahādvipau vāśitāsaṃgame dṛptau śaradīva madotkaṭau
english: They rushed upon each other like two great elephants in rut, frenzied as in autumn, proud at the meeting over a she-elephant.

sanskrit: mattāv iva jigīṣantau mātaṅgau bharatarṣabhau ubhau krodhaviṣaṃ dīptaṃ vamantāv uragāv iva
english: Those two bulls of the Bhāratas, eager for victory like two maddened elephants, spat forth the blazing venom of their wrath like two serpents.

sanskrit: anyonyam abhisaṃrabdhau prekṣamāṇāv ariṃdamau ubhau bharataśārdūlau vikrameṇa samanvitau
english: Furious at each other, those two tamers of foes glared, both tigers among the Bhāratas, endowed with valor.

sanskrit: siṃhāv iva durādharṣau gadāyuddhe paraṃtapau nakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhau vīrau vyāghrāv iva durutsahau
english: Unassailable as two lions, those scorchers of foes in mace-combat, the heroes were hard to withstand as two tigers armed with claws and fangs.

sanskrit: prajāsaṃharaṇe kṣubdhau samudrāv iva dustarau lohitāṅgāv iva kruddhau pratapantau mahārathau
english: They were like two oceans hard to cross, churned at the destruction of all creatures; and the two great chariot-warriors blazed in their fury like two angry red-bodied planets of Mars.
